series: trendwatching.com annual consumer trends (free Trend Briefing)
title: trendwatching.com's TOP 5 CONSUMER TRENDS FOR 2007
notes: January 2007 Trend Briefing; first year list ('we've finally succumbed to list mania'). Labels are the numbered heading images' alt text. target_year 2007 from the title. The paid 2007 Trend Report (CD-ROM/download) is not captured.

entries.label: STATUS LIFESTYLES
entries.quote: expect 2007 to be the year in which many brands realize (if not grudgingly accept) that the ‘old’, mass-era status symbols, from the Audi Q7 to the De Beers Radiance collection, are no longer every consumers’ wet dream.
entries.subject: Status beyond traditional consumption (experience, participation, connection, eco status)
entries.note: Sub-lifestyles listed: TRANSIENT, PARTICIPATIVE, CONNECTING (part of ONLINE), ECO-LIFESTYLES.

entries.label: TRANSPARENCY TYRANNY
entries.quote: 2007 could be the year in which TRANSPARENCY TYRANNY really starts scaring the shit out of non-performing brands.
entries.subject: Consumer reviews and price/opinion transparency online
entries.note: Sub-themes: multimedia and real-time reviews, PROFILE MANIA, paid contributors, niche price comparison, group buying (CROWD CLOUT).

entries.label: WEB N+1
entries.quote: 2007 will see a broad debate on what constitutes web 3.0, web 4.0 and who knows, even web 5.0.
entries.subject: Next phases of the web (mobile web, internet of things, metaverse)

entries.label: TRYSUMERS
entries.quote: experienced consumers are trying out new appliances, new services, new flavors, new authors, new destinations, new artists, new relationships, new *anything* with post mass-market gusto.
entries.subject: Experimental, adventurous consumption
entries.note: Quote is part of the edition's 'beta-definition' of TRYSUMERS.

entries.label: THE GLOBAL BRAIN
entries.quote: This year, expect many corporations, small and big, to aggressively court the 1% of most creative and experienced individuals roaming the globe.
entries.subject: Companies co-creating with skilled consumers (crowdsourcing)
